statement.p: Let f(x,y) = 1+3x^{2}-\cos\mathopen{}\left(4y\right). Find all critical points and classify them as local maxima, local minima, saddle points, or none of these.

p.em: (give your points as a comma separated list of (x,y) coordinates. if your answer includes points that occur at a sequence of values, e.g., at every odd integer, or at any constant multiple of another value, use m for any non-zero even integer, n for any non-zero odd integer, and/or k for other arbitrary constants.)
(give your answers in a comma separated list, specifying maximum, minimum, saddle point, or none for each, in the same order as you entered your critical points)

static.solution:
f_x = 6 x = 0 and f_y = 4\sin(4 y) = 0. The first equation has solution x = 0, and the second equation, y = n\pi/4 (where n is any integer). Thus our critical points are (0,0), (0,\frac{m\pi}{4}), and (0,\frac{n\pi}{4}) (where m is any non-zero even integer and n is any non-zero odd integer).
We calculate D=(f_{xx})(f_{yy})-(f_{xy})^2 = (6)(16 \cos(4 y)) - (0)^2. Thus, at (0,0), D > 0 and f_{xx} > 0, so this is a \text{minimum}. Similarly, at (0,\frac{m\pi}{4}), D > 0 and f_{xx} > 0, so this is a \text{minimum}, and at (0,\frac{n\pi}{4}), D \lt 0, so this is a \text{saddle point},
